title: Redwood Optimize walkthrough - batching & KV prefix cache (Fintrix Payments)
next_steps: Share optimized costing spreadsheet + batching calculator
Follow up on network/VPC questions with engineering notes
action_items: Jamie Cole: Send pricing and optimized cost model spreadsheet (due: 2026-07-23)
Priya Shah: Prepare pilot run outline and perf test plan (due: 2026-07-30)
Marco Li: Share Terraform snippet for VPC peering + KMS notes (due: 2026-07-26)
Lena Ortiz (Fintrix): Confirm list of allowed IPs and compliance contacts (due: 2026-07-24)
summary: Redwood SE team walked Fintrix Payments through Optimize recommendations focusing on batching strategies and prefix/KV cache to reduce token costs and meet sub-200ms SLOs for short flows. Discussed tradeoffs, dedicated vs hosted, and pilot next steps.
transcript:
14:00 Jamie (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intro - I'm Jamie on the account team, joined by Priya and Marco from SE.
14:12 Alex (CTO): Hey thanks, Alex here, Sara and Devon and Lena on our side. we're excited to see the optimize walkthrough.
14:20 Jamie: Great - objective today is to run through batching and KV/prefix cache recommendations, show the cost model, and agree a pilot. We'll move a bit fast but stop for Qs.
14:35 Priya (SE): Quick context: Fintrix told us typical flows are payment auth and reconciliation summaries - short prompts, many repeated prefixes (transaction templates). Sequence lengths average 80-120 tokens but with a 20% tail up to 600 for some reconciliations.
14:52 Sara (Head ML): Yes that's accurate. We care about latency for auth path (sub-200ms ideally) and want to cut token costs on reconciliation where latency tolerance is higher.
15:05 Marco (SE): Ok, so two knobs: batching to increase GPU utilization on longer workloads and prefix/KV cache to avoid re-processing the same system/prompt prefixes. We'll show numbers.
15:20 Priya: First, batching. If you have bursts of concurrent short requests, small batching windows (5-20ms) can group requests and reduce per-token overhead. There's a sweet spot - too much batching hurts p95 latency.
15:38 Devon (Infra): What does that look like for our traffic pattern? We have spikes around 10k reqs/minute during settlement windows.
15:45 Priya: With your QPS, we recommend mixed policies: a latency-first route for auth (no batching / very small window) and a cost-first route for reconciliation (longer batching, up to 50ms or 100ms depending on SLO).
16:02 Jamie: We'll show the cost delta. Marco, can you pull up the spreadsheet?
16:06 Marco: Yep - sharing screen (link in chat: https://redwood.ai/decks/fintrix-optimize).
16:15 Marco: Baseline: hosted API, no caching, conservative batching defaults - cost X. With KV/prefix cache for repeated 60-token prefixes we see token reduction ~40-60% on those flows. Combined with batching on reconciliation, net token cost reduction for that route ~55% in this model.
16:40 Alex: 55% is promising, what assumptions on cache hit rate?
16:44 Marco: Good question - this model uses hit rates of 70% for the reconciliation templates (they're very repetitive). For auth path we assume ~10% hit (less repetitive). We can parameterize.
16:58 Sara: How does cache size and eviction affect accuracy? We're worried about staleness and hallucination if prefix content changes.
17:05 Priya: Cache keys are deterministic on the prefix text + model/version + routing config. If you change system prompts or update model version, you invalidate the key. We also support TTLs and versioned prefixes. Eviction is LRU by token length/usage to control memory.
17:24 Lena (Security): From security side, what data leaves our VPC? Is cached content stored encrypted?
17:31 Marco: For Private and Dedicated deployments, cache lives in customer-controlled VPC and can be encrypted with your KMS/HSM. For hosted we store encrypted at rest with customer tenancy separation. We'll send the KMS integration doc.
17:46 Lena: Okay please include SOC2 and key rotation notes.
17:50 Jamie: Noted. We'll attach compliance pack.
17:56 Priya: Back to batching+latency - one pattern we recommend is hybrid routing: route auth to a sub-200ms optimized pool (lower batch sizes, higher priority), route heavy reconciliation to a cost-optimized pool with larger batching and KV cache. This can be done via per-route policies in the Redwood Console.
18:16 Alex: If we split routes, how does capacity planning work? We don't want auth pool to run out and degrade p99.
18:25 Priya: We recommend reserved capacity for the auth pool (Redwood Dedicated) sized to p99 traffic plus headroom, with auto-bursting to hosted capacity as fallback. That guarantees SLO and lets cost optimize the other route.
18:40 Devon: For the pilot, we'd probably want to test both hosted and dedicated to compare.
18:45 Marco: Absolutely - pilot plan we suggested includes a 2-hour perf run on your sample traffic to estimate real-world hit rates, latency distribution, and cost. We'll instrument token-level telemetry and share a cost breakdown.
19:02 Sara: How do we measure accuracy/regression when using cache? If we reuse KV cached outputs, could that hide subtle regressions after model rollouts?
19:12 Priya: Good point. We recommend cache invalidation tied to model rollouts and also A/B sampling (we keep a small percent of requests uncached to compare outputs). Redwood Optimize has built-in evaluation hooks to detect drift/regressions based on your prompt sets.
19:35 Alex: Is there an easy way to simulate cost vs latency tradeoff?
19:40 Marco: Yes the spreadsheet has sliders for hit rate, batch window, and sequence length distribution - it outputs estimate unit cost and latency p50/p95. We'll send the editable sheet.
19:52 Jamie: Quick demo: toggling batch window from 5ms to 50ms increases average throughput 2.1x but p95 latency for small auth requests goes from 160ms to 320ms, so you can see the tradeoff.
20:12 Devon: Any guidance on kernel/quantization settings? We use Ampere A100 and some T4s in prod.
20:20 Priya: For A100s we recommend int8 or q4 variants for cost-heavy reconciliation models. For auth (latency-critical) we prefer FP16 where possible to minimize latency variance. The runtime will pick kernels; we can recommend model variants and quant profiles per route.
20:41 Sara: And for sequence lengths that spike to 600? Will batching hurt those long-tail requests?
20:48 Priya: Long sequences are batched separately with dynamic batching that accounts for KV cache size. Long-tail requests often benefit less from batching because they dominate GPU time, so we isolate them with their own pool to avoid impacting short request latency.
21:10 Alex: About implementation: how invasive is integration? We use house-built API gateway and a mix of Lambda + GKE services.
21:18 Marco: Integration is via our REST API/SDK. For Private deployments we provide a control plane plus a connector you run in your VPC. For quick pilots, the hosted API is simplest - you can route specific endpoints to Redwood and keep others internal. We also provide Terraform snippets for VPC peering which I will share.
21:36 Lena: Any notes on audit logs for cache reads/writes? We need per-request auditability.
21:42 Marco: Yes we log cache hits/misses, request ids, and basic metadata; for Private deployments logs can be exported to your SIEM. Logs do not include raw PII by default - we can customize.
22:00 Priya: Wrapping up the cost model: combined approach (route split + KV/prefix cache + batching) typically yields 40-70% cost reduction on repetitive workloads in our customers. Your spreadsheet preview shows a midpoint ~55% given your traffic assumptions.
22:20 Sara: Sounds good. Could you show a sample latency/cost table for a 24-hour window?
22:26 Marco: (shares table in chat) - we project auth route cost $Y/day, p50 120ms, p95 180ms; reconciliation route cost drop from $Z to $Z*0.45 with p50 rising but p95 still acceptable. Exact numbers tied to pilot results.
22:50 Alex: Any licence or enterprise pricing constraints? We have a procurement cycle.
22:56 Jamie: We'll include pricing tiers in the doc, with Dedicated reserved capacity commit for auth and usage-based for other routes. We'll also include procurement checklist.
23:10 Sara: On next steps - pilot data sharing needs a data access agreement?
23:15 Jamie: We'll send a short pilot agreement and the SOC2 + KMS docs.
23:21 Devon: For the pilot, we want a perf run that includes our spike windows; would 8/4 in the morning PST work?
23:28 Jamie: We'll propose 8/4 9am PT in the follow-up.
23:32 Lena: Please cc our security contact on the compliance email.
23:36 Jamie: Will do.
23:40 Alex: Ok quick recap?
23:42 Jamie: Recap - send cost spreadsheet + pricing, send security/compliance pack, schedule 2-hour pilot perf run (week of 8/3), share Terraform + VPC/KMS snippets, and SE team will run the perf instrumentation and share results.
23:58 Sara: Thanks team, this was useful.
24:05 Priya: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up with action items and the links.
24:12 (end)
